**BLUF:** You can mention the AI‑built app—include it in the cover letter, but keep it short and tie it to product design skills. ❯

---  

**Cover Letter (Junior Product Designer, Monzo)**  

[Your Name]  
[Address] | [Phone] | [Email] | [Portfolio URL]  

[Date]

Hiring Team – Monzo  
[Monzo Address]

Dear Hiring Team,

I’m excited to apply for the Junior Product Designer position at Monzo. With two years of barista experience and a self‑taught command of Figma, I bring a customer‑first mindset and a fresh, approachable design perspective to your team.

**Why I fit Monzo**

* **People‑centred service** – As a barista, I consistently turned first‑time customers into regulars by listening to their preferences and delivering personalized service. I translate this empathy into design, ensuring every feature solves real user needs.
* **Rapid prototyping in Figma** – I built a simple AI‑guided mobile app prototype (for a personal project) that accepted user preferences and suggested coffee orders. Though still a prototype, it taught me how to iterate quickly, test with users, and refine both UI and UX based on real feedback.
* **Self‑directed learning** – I spent months mastering Figma, UI kits, and design systems independently. I’m comfortable diving into Monzo’s design guidelines and can contribute fresh design concepts while aligning with your visual identity.

**Portfolio Highlight**

I’d love to share a live prototype I built that demonstrates my understanding of user flows and Figma’s component system. It includes an AI suggestion module—showing my ability to integrate emerging tech into user experience.

Thank you for considering my application. I’m eager to discuss how my background and passion for inclusive design can support Monzo’s mission to make banking simple and friendly.

Sincerely,

[Your Name]  

---  

**Quick Q&A**

*Is it ok to mention I built an app with AI?*  
Yes – it showcases initiative and technical curiosity. Just keep the description brief and focus on how it reflects design thinking, user testing, and iterative improvement.
